Multiply nonnegative radicands under one square root. Principal roots are nonnegative.
Square root two times square root eight equals square root sixteen, which is four.
Square root six times square root fifteen is square root ninety, or three square root ten.
Two square root three times four square root six becomes eight square root eighteen, or twenty-four square root two.
For nonnegative x, square root three x times square root twelve x is six x. In general, square root x squared is absolute x.
Multiply square root five plus square root two by square root five, obtaining five plus square root ten.
A sum times its difference equals the difference of squares. Here five minus two equals three.
If x is at least one half, multiplying square roots of two x plus one and two x minus one gives square root fifteen only when x equals two. Square both sides and check the domain.
